bw: Nephrotic syndrome with renal vein thrombosis
cards.tp: Heavy proteinuria loses antithrombin III (and protein C/S), causing hypercoagulability and renal vein thrombosis; membranous nephropathy is the classic cause.

ww.Antiphospholipid antibodies: Antiphospholipid antibodies cause thrombosis but not heavy proteinuria.
ww.Impaired estrogen degradation: Estrogen degradation is not impaired in nephrotic syndrome.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Loss of antithrombin III.

cards.tp: Pemphigus vulgaris: IgG against desmoglein 3 (cadherin) causes acantholysis. Bullous pemphigoid targets hemidesmosomes (collagen XVII).

ww.Integrin: Integrins anchor cells at hemidesmosomes, targeted in bullous pemphigoid.
ww.Collagen: Collagen VII is the target in epidermolysis bullosa acquisita.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Cadherin.

bw: Knee arthroplasty wound with yellow-green discharge
cards.tp: Necrotizing or deep wound infection needs prompt debridement plus antibiotics; implant removal is considered if infection involves the prosthesis.

ww.Nafcillin therapy: Nafcillin alone cannot control necrotic infected tissue.
ww.Antiseptic dressing\n\": Antiseptic dressings do not remove devitalized tissue.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Surgical debridement.

bw: Influenza within 48 hours in a high-risk patient
cards.tp: Neuraminidase inhibitors reduce symptom duration if started early and are recommended for high-risk patients (asthma, pregnancy, age over 65); amantadine is not recommended due to resistance.

ww.Amantadine: Amantadine is no longer recommended because of widespread resistance.
ww.Supportive care only: Supportive care alone may be insufficient for a high-risk patient such as an asthmatic.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Oseltamivir.

bw: Vaginal mass in an HPV-positive postmenopausal woman
cards.tp: Most vaginal cancers are HPV-related squamous cell carcinomas; sarcoma botryoides (embryonal rhabdomyosarcoma) occurs in young girls.

ww.Sarcoma botryoides: Sarcoma botryoides is a vaginal tumor of young girls.
ww.Melanoma: Vaginal melanoma is rare and causes pigmented lesions.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Squamous cell carcinoma.

bw: Brief LOC, normal ECG and labs
cards.tp: Situational syncope follows micturition, defecation, cough or swallowing through vagal stimulation; evaluation is usually reassuring.

ww.Emotional syncope: Emotional syncope is triggered by fear or distress rather than micturition.
ww.Arrhythmogenic syncope: Arrhythmogenic syncope has abnormal ECG findings or cardiac history.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Situational syncope.

bw: Best bedside marker of adequate fluids?
cards.tp: Titrate burn fluids to urine output (about 0.5 mL/kg/h in adults); the Parkland formula only gives the starting rate.

ww.Blood pressure: Blood pressure stays normal until late in burn shock and is an insensitive guide.
ww.Pulmonary capillary wedge pressure: Wedge pressure needs a pulmonary artery catheter and is not used to titrate burn fluids.

cards.evidence:
The keyed answer is D) Urinary output
".

bw: SLE with pleuritic chest pain and friction rub
cards.tp: Serositis is common in lupus (pericarditis, pleuritis); pericarditis causes positional pain relieved by leaning forward, diffuse ST elevation and PR depression.

ww.Pericardial tamponade: Tamponade causes hypotension, muffled heart sounds and JVD.
ww.Acute myocardial infarction: MI shows localized ST changes and a troponin rise.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Pericarditis.

bw: Facial swelling and dark urine after a sore throat
cards.tp: Poststreptococcal glomerulonephritis: nephritic syndrome with RBC casts, low C3, hypertension and edema, 1-3 weeks after pharyngitis.

ww.WBC casts: WBC casts indicate pyelonephritis or interstitial nephritis.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) RBC casts.

cards.tp: Plaque psoriasis is a clinical diagnosis: well-demarcated erythematous plaques with silvery scale and the Auspitz sign.

ww.Skin biopsy: Biopsy is reserved for atypical or uncertain presentations.
ww.Wood’s lamp: A Wood's lamp detects fluorescence of some fungal and bacterial infections.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) No tests are necessary.

cards.tp: Postmenopausal bleeding needs exclusion of endometrial cancer by office biopsy or transvaginal ultrasound; risks include obesity, unopposed estrogen and PCOS history.

ww.Hysteroscopy with D&C: Hysteroscopy with D&C is more invasive and used if the biopsy is inadequate.
ww.Saline infusion sonography: Saline infusion sonography evaluates focal lesions after a nondiagnostic evaluation.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Endometrial biopsy.

cards.tp: Recombination (chiasmata) occurs in prophase I of meiosis, generating genetic diversity.
cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Prophase I.

bw: Acute mania with chronic kidney disease
cards.tp: Lithium is renally cleared and nephrotoxic, so avoid it in renal impairment. Valproate is hepatically metabolized and antimanic; lamotrigine is not effective for acute mania.

ww.Lithium: Lithium is renally cleared and nephrotoxic, so it is avoided in renal impairment.
ww.Lamotrigine: Lamotrigine does not treat acute mania.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Valproic acid.

cards.tp: Macrophages express CD14 (LPS receptor); CD4 T helper cells surround the granuloma and secrete IFN-gamma to activate macrophages.
cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) CD14.

cards.tp: Anticholinergic toxidrome: 'hot as a hare, dry as a bone, blind as a bat, mad as a hatter'; physostigmine reverses it, but avoid in TCA overdose.
cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Physostigmine.

bw: Reversed by IV drug: which receptor?
cards.tp: Naloxone is a competitive mu-opioid antagonist reversing opioid overdose; flumazenil acts at GABA-A for benzodiazepines.

ww.GABA-A receptor: Flumazenil acts at GABA-A to reverse benzodiazepines.
ww.5-HT2A receptor: 5-HT2A is the receptor targeted by LSD and some antipsychotics.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) μ-receptor.

d: Decreased sensation of the anterior thigh
cards.tp: S1 compression gives plantarflexion weakness, reduced ankle jerk and lateral foot sensory loss; L4 affects the patellar reflex and L5 causes foot drop.

ww.Exaggerated patellar reflex: Exaggerated reflexes indicate an upper motor neuron lesion, not root compression.
ww.Decreased sensation of the anterior thig: Anterior thigh sensation is supplied by L2-L3, not S1.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Weak achilles tendon reflex.

bw: Pregnant woman seizing with BP 186/97 and RUQ pain
cards.tp: Eclampsia is treated with magnesium sulfate for seizure control and prophylaxis, plus blood pressure control; delivery follows maternal stabilization.

ww.Emergency cesarean section: Cesarean delivery follows maternal stabilization and does not stop the seizure.
ww.IV oxytocin: Oxytocin induces labor but does not treat an eclamptic seizure.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Intravenous magnesium sulfate.

cards.tp: Leucovorin (folinic acid) bypasses dihydrofolate reductase blockade and rescues cells from methotrexate toxicity.

ww.Amifostine: Amifostine protects against cisplatin renal toxicity and radiation xerostomia.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Leucovorin.

cards.tp: Dystrophinopathy (Becker or Duchenne) is confirmed by dystrophin gene testing (deletion/duplication analysis); biopsy is no longer first line.

ww.Electromyography: EMG shows a myopathic pattern but does not confirm the specific diagnosis.
ww.Tensilon test: The Tensilon test is for myasthenia gravis.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Genetic analysis.

cards.tp: Disc herniation compresses lumbosacral roots (L5/S1 most often), causing radicular pain below the knee; bilateral deficits with saddle numbness suggest cauda equina syndrome.

ww.Vertebral body compromise: Vertebral fracture or metastasis causes focal pain with systemic signs.
ww.Inflammatory spinal degeneration: Spondyloarthritis gives morning stiffness in young men, not post-lifting sciatica.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Herniation of nucleus pulposus into vertebral canal.

cards.tp: Neprilysin degrades natriuretic peptides and bradykinin; sacubitril (with valsartan) treats heart failure. Do not combine with ACE inhibitors (angioedema).

ww.Nitric oxide: Nitric oxide is not raised by neprilysin inhibition.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Natriuretic peptides.

bw: Itchy facial rash in a wheezy toddler
cards.tp: Atopic dermatitis (eczema) is part of the atopic triad with asthma and allergic rhinitis; infants have facial and extensor involvement.

ww.Viral conjunctivitis: Viral conjunctivitis causes watery red eyes without a periorbital rash.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Atopic dermatitis.

d: Inherited abnormalities in type IV collagen
cards.tp: IgA nephropathy (Berger) causes hematuria 1-2 days after a respiratory infection (synpharyngitic), with normal complement.

ww.Inherited abnormalities in type IV colla: Alport syndrome is a type IV collagen defect with deafness and a family history, not a post-infectious flare.
ww.Immune complex deposition: Immune complex deposition with low C3 follows strep infection after 1 to 3 weeks.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Diffuse mesangial IgA deposition.

bw: Graves disease in a pregnant woman
cards.tp: Radioiodine is contraindicated in pregnancy; PTU is used in the first trimester (methimazole teratogenic), then methimazole later. Beta-blockers help symptoms short term.

ww.Radioactive iodine: Radioactive iodine is contraindicated in pregnancy.
ww.Levothyroxine: Levothyroxine treats hypothyroidism, not Graves hyperthyroidism.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Thyroid peroxidase inhibitors.

cards.tp: Chromosomes are most condensed and visible in metaphase; colchicine arrests cells there for karyotype preparation (47,XX+21).

ww.S phase: S phase is DNA synthesis, not condensed chromosomes.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Metaphase.

bw: BPH drug causing first-dose orthostatic syncope
cards.tp: Tamsulosin, terazosin and doxazosin relax prostatic smooth muscle but cause orthostatic hypotension, worst with the first dose; start at bedtime.

ww.Alpha-2 adrenergic agonist: Alpha-2 agonists act centrally and do not relax the prostate.
ww.Muscarinic agonist: Muscarinic agonists contract the bladder and worsen retention.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Alpha-1-adrenergic receptor antagonist.

bw: Spatial distribution of CD117 cells in tissue
cards.tp: IHC stains protein in tissue sections, preserving architecture; GISTs are CD117 (KIT) positive and respond to imatinib.

ww.Northern blot: Northern blot detects RNA and does not show tissue distribution.
ww.Flow cytometry: Flow cytometry measures cell populations in suspension, not tissue architecture.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Immunohistochemistry.

bw: Lace-like rash with circumoral pallor in a child
cards.tp: Parvovirus B19 (erythema infectiosum, fifth disease) infects erythroid precursors via P antigen, causing aplastic crisis in hemolytic anemias and hydrops fetalis.

ww.T lymphocytes: T lymphocytes are infected by HIV and HTLV.
ww.Monocytes: Monocytes are infected by CMV and HIV, not parvovirus.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Erythroid progenitor cells.

cards.tp: Mycoplasma pneumoniae (cholesterol-containing membrane, no cell wall, cold agglutinins) responds to macrolides, doxycycline or fluoroquinolones.

ww.Intravenous ceftriaxone: Ceftriaxone is ineffective because Mycoplasma lacks a cell wall.
ww.Oral amoxicillin: Amoxicillin is a beta-lactam and does not work against organisms without a cell wall.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Oral azithromycin.

cards.tp: Leukotrienes C4, D4 and E4 cause potent, prolonged bronchoconstriction in asthma; montelukast blocks the CysLT1 receptor, zileuton blocks 5-lipoxygenase.

ww.Bradykinin: Bradykinin causes pain and vasodilation, not the main asthma bronchoconstrictor.
ww.Serotonin: Serotonin is not a central mediator of asthma.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Leukotrienes.

bw: Virilized newborn girl, maternal hirsutism in pregnancy
cards.tp: Aromatase deficiency blocks conversion of androgens to estrogens, causing fetal and maternal virilization and lack of puberty with high gonadotropins.

ww.Polycystic ovary syndrome: PCOS does not cause genital virilization at birth or absent breast development.
ww.Congenital adrenal hyperplasia: Congenital adrenal hyperplasia virilizes the fetus but the mother is not virilized in pregnancy, and ovaries are not cystic from lack of estrogen.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Aromatase deficiency.

bw: High IgE and IgA, low IgM
cards.tp: Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome (WAS gene, X-linked): the triad of eczema, recurrent infections and thrombocytopenia with small platelets; treat with bone marrow transplant.

ww.NADPH oxidase deficiency: NADPH oxidase deficiency is chronic granulomatous disease.
ww.Leukopenia: Leukopenia is not characteristic of Wiskott-Aldrich syndrome.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Thrombocytopenia.

cards.tp: Cesarean at 38 weeks plus intrapartum zidovudine reduces transmission when viral load exceeds 1000 copies/mL; vaginal delivery is acceptable if suppressed.

ww.Increase AZT dose: Increasing the AZT dose does not suppress the viral load enough.
ww.Add nevirapine: Intrapartum nevirapine is an older single-dose option with resistance risk.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Urge the patient to have a cesarean section delivery.

cards.tp: Wet AMD is treated with intravitreal anti-VEGF agents (bevacizumab, ranibizumab, aflibercept). Corneal cross-linking treats keratoconus.
cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Inhibit choroidal neovascularization.

cards.tp: Glomus tumors arise from glomus body cells (modified smooth muscle) controlling temperature regulation, and are exquisitely tender and cold-sensitive.

ww.Dysplastic melanocytes: Dysplastic melanocytes produce nevi or melanoma, not tender subungual papules.
ww.Injured nerve cells: Injured nerve cells form traumatic neuromas, not cold-sensitive blue papules.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Modified smooth muscle cells.

cards.tp: ODD: at least 6 months of negativistic, hostile, defiant behavior toward authority without serious violations of others' rights, unlike conduct disorder.

ww.Conduct disorder: Conduct disorder involves violating others' rights and rules.
ww.ADHD: ADHD causes inattention and hyperactivity rather than targeted defiance.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Oppositional defiant disorder.

bw: Tricuspid regurgitation murmur louder on inspiration
cards.tp: Inspiration increases venous return to the right heart and RV stroke volume, intensifying right-sided murmurs (Carvallo sign); left-sided murmurs soften.

ww.Increased peripheral vascular resistance: Increased systemic resistance would worsen left-sided murmurs such as mitral regurgitation.
ww.Increased systemic venous compliance: Venous compliance does not explain the inspiratory increase.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Increased right ventricular stroke volume.

cards.tp: Secondary prophylaxis of variceal bleeding combines nonselective beta-blockers (propranolol, nadolol) with repeated endoscopic band ligation.

ww.Octreotide: Octreotide is used for acute bleeding, not long-term prophylaxis.
ww.TIPS: TIPS is rescue therapy for failed endoscopic and medical management.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Variceal ligation.

bw: Muscle supplied by the injured nerve?
cards.tp: The axillary nerve (C5-C6) supplies deltoid and teres minor, and gives sensation over the lateral shoulder. Supraspinatus is suprascapular nerve; subscapularis is the subscapular nerves.

ww.Supraspinatus: Supraspinatus is supplied by the suprascapular nerve.
ww.Subscapularis: Subscapularis is supplied by the upper and lower subscapular nerves.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Teres minor.

bw: Cape-like pain and temperature loss in both arms
cards.tp: A syrinx (syringomyelia) interrupts spinothalamic fibers crossing in the ventral white commissure. Dorsal column (vibration, cuneate fasciculus) is spared.

ww.Cuneate fasciculus: The cuneate fasciculus carries upper limb vibration and proprioception, which are spared.
ww.Anterior corticospinal tract: The anterior corticospinal tract controls motor function, not sensation.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Ventral white commissure.

bw: Healthy toddler with a harsh holosystolic murmur
cards.tp: VSD is the most common congenital heart defect, usually membranous; small defects are asymptomatic and often close spontaneously, large ones cause shunting and heart failure.

ww.Muscular interventricular septum: Muscular septal defects are less common and often close.
ww.Endocardial cushion: Endocardial cushion defects cause AV septal defects, common in Down syndrome.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Defect of the membranous interventricular septum.

cards.tp: A vascular ring encircles the trachea and esophagus, causing stridor and dysphagia; barium swallow shows indentation. Laryngomalacia is typically better when prone.

ww.Laryngomalacia: Laryngomalacia improves when the infant is prone and does not cause vomiting.
ww.Congenital subglottic stenosis: Subglottic stenosis causes persistent stridor not changing with neck position.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Double aortic arch.

cards.tp: Atypical hyperplasia usually warrants hysterectomy, but fertility-sparing progestin therapy with close monitoring is used if pregnancy is desired.

ww.Hysterectomy and salpingo-oophorectomy: Hysterectomy ends fertility and is standard once childbearing is complete.
ww.Observation with annual biopsy: Observation is inadequate because atypical hyperplasia can progress to cancer.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Start progestin-only therapy.

cards.tp: SSRIs are first-line because of safety and tolerability; benzodiazepines do not treat depression and TCAs are dangerous in overdose.

ww.Diazepam: Benzodiazepines do not treat depression and carry dependence risk.
ww.Amitriptyline: Amitriptyline is a TCA with anticholinergic effects and overdose toxicity.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Escitalopram therapy.

bw: Neonate with high ammonia, high orotic acid
cards.tp: OTC deficiency (X-linked) blocks the urea cycle: ammonia and orotic acid rise with low citrulline. Treat with sodium benzoate/phenylacetate, protein restriction, arginine or citrulline.

ww.Uridine: Uridine treats hereditary orotic aciduria, which has normal ammonia.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Benzoate administration.

bw: Unvaccinated child stays healthy because community is immune
cards.tp: When enough people are vaccinated, transmission falls and protects the unvaccinated; thresholds depend on R0 (about 95 percent for measles).

ww.Immune evasion: Immune evasion refers to pathogens escaping host immunity.
ww.Tolerance: Tolerance is the lack of response to self antigens.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Herd immunity.

bw: Radial wrist pain holding an infant
Pain with ulnar deviation of fist
cards.tp: De Quervain tenosynovitis (abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis) is positive on Finkelstein test; treat with thumb spica splint and NSAIDs.

ww.Carpal tunnel syndrome: Carpal tunnel syndrome causes median nerve paresthesias, not radial wrist pain over the tendons.
ww.Mallet finger: Mallet finger is a distal phalanx extensor tendon avulsion.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) De Quervain tenosynovitis.

cards.tp: Always exclude pregnancy first in a patient with amenorrhea and compatible symptoms, even when menarche has not occurred.

ww.Prolactin: Prolactin excess causes amenorrhea but not nausea and a pregnancy picture.
ww.Thyrotropin: Thyrotropin would not explain nausea, urinary frequency and breast tenderness first.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Human chorionic gonadotropin.

bw: Strongest maternal risk factor for early pregnancy loss?
cards.tp: Most first-trimester losses are chromosomal aneuploidy, rising with maternal age; risk exceeds 30 percent after 40.

ww.Chronic hypertension: Chronic hypertension raises preeclampsia risk more than early loss.
ww.Hypercoagulable state: Hypercoagulability is linked to recurrent loss, but most early losses are chromosomal.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Age.

cards.tp: Sicca syndrome (dry eyes and mouth) with anti-Ro/La. Anti-CCP is rheumatoid arthritis; anti-Scl-70 is diffuse systemic sclerosis.

ww.Anti-CCP: Anti-CCP antibodies are specific for rheumatoid arthritis.
ww.Anti-topoisomerase I (Scl-70): Anti-Scl-70 (topoisomerase I) marks diffuse systemic sclerosis.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Anti-SS-B (anti-La) antibodies.

cards.tp: HbS (Glu6Val) and HbC (Glu6Lys) heterozygosity protect against P. falciparum; G6PD deficiency and thalassemia also confer some protection.

ww.ALAS2 gene defect: ALAS2 defects cause X-linked sideroblastic anemia and do not protect against malaria.
ww.Diamond-Blackfan ribosomal defect: Diamond-Blackfan anemia is a ribosomal protein defect causing red cell aplasia.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Glutamic acid substitution in the β-globin chain.

cards.tp: Acute HBV can start with a serum-sickness-like prodrome (immune complexes: rash, arthralgia) before jaundice. HAV does not cause this prodrome.

ww.Hepatitis A: Hepatitis A does not cause a serum-sickness-like prodrome.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Hepatitis B.

cards.tp: Infantile seborrheic dermatitis (cradle cap) is benign and self-limited; emollients and gentle shampoos help.

ww.Atopic dermatitis: Atopic dermatitis is intensely itchy and spares the scalp's greasy scale pattern in infants.
ww.Allergic contact dermatitis: Allergic contact dermatitis follows exposure to an allergen and is vesicular and pruritic.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Seborrheic dermatitis.

bw: Fever days after central line placement
cards.tp: CLABSI is diagnosed by matching organisms in blood drawn from the line and peripherally; remove the line and treat, often with vancomycin.

ww.Catheter-associated urinary tract infect: Catheter-associated UTI would show urine cultures rather than line cultures.
ww.Surgical site infection: Surgical site infection would be local to the sternotomy or leg wound.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Central line-associated blood stream infection.

cards.tp: Bioprosthetic valves degrade over 10-15 years and need replacement; mechanical valves last longer but require lifelong warfarin.

ww.Prosthetic valve endocarditis: Endocarditis would cause fever and embolic phenomena.
ww.Pulmonary embolism: Pulmonary embolism presents with sudden dyspnea and pleuritic pain, not a new diastolic murmur.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Valve degeneration.

bw: Which diabetes drug raises C-peptide levels?
cards.tp: Sulfonylureas close beta-cell K-ATP channels, increasing insulin and C-peptide release. Exogenous insulin suppresses C-peptide.

ww.Acarbose: Acarbose blocks intestinal alpha-glucosidase and does not raise insulin.
ww.Exogenous insulin: Exogenous insulin suppresses endogenous insulin and C-peptide.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Glipizide.

cards.tp: Dopamine agonists (cabergoline, bromocriptine) suppress prolactin and shrink prolactinomas; metoclopramide is a D2 antagonist that raises prolactin.

ww.Estrogen: Estrogen does not lower prolactin and can stimulate prolactinomas.
ww.Metoclopramide: Metoclopramide is a D2 antagonist that raises prolactin.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Bromocriptine.

bw: Garlic breath and QT prolongation after termite poison
cards.tp: Arsenic poisoning causes GI symptoms, garlic odor and QT prolongation; chelate with dimercaprol (BAL) or DMSA. Deferoxamine is for iron; NAC for acetaminophen.
cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Dimercaprol.

cards.tp: Secondary prophylaxis after rheumatic fever with residual valve disease continues for at least 10 years since the last attack or until age 40.

ww.Stop penicillin in 4 years: Secondary prophylaxis with valve disease lasts at least 10 years or until about age 40, so stopping at 25 is too early.
ww.Switch to cefotaxime: Cefotaxime is not the standard agent; penicillin G remains first line.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Continue intramuscular penicillin therapy.

cards.tp: Tetracyclines chelate calcium and deposit in bone and teeth: avoid in pregnancy and children under 8.

ww.Atrialization of the ventricle: Atrialization of the right ventricle (Ebstein anomaly) follows lithium.
ww.Gray coloring of the skin: Gray baby syndrome follows chloramphenicol in neonates.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Inhibition of bone growth.

cards.tp: Somatostatin analogs (octreotide, lanreotide) lower GH and IGF-1; pegvisomant blocks the GH receptor; transsphenoidal surgery is first line.

ww.Metyrapone: Metyrapone blocks cortisol synthesis in Cushing syndrome.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Octreotide.

cards.tp: Phenytoin: gingival hyperplasia, hirsutism, nystagmus, megaloblastic anemia, teratogenic fetal hydantoin syndrome, and CYP450 induction.

ww.Lamotrigine: Lamotrigine causes rash and Stevens-Johnson syndrome.
ww.Carbamazepine: Carbamazepine causes hyponatremia, aplastic anemia and neural tube defects.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Phenytoin.

cards.tp: Intrauterine fetal demise at 24-26 weeks is managed with induction of labor (misoprostol or oxytocin) for vaginal delivery.

ww.Perform cesarean delivery: Cesarean adds maternal morbidity and is avoided in intrauterine fetal demise.
ww.Perform dilation and curettage\n\": Dilation and curettage is for early pregnancy loss before the second trimester.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Plan for oxytocin administration.

bw: Adolescent ovarian mass with elevated beta-hCG and AFP
cards.tp: Embryonal carcinoma secretes both hCG and AFP; yolk sac tumors secrete AFP (Schiller-Duval bodies); dysgerminoma has LDH.

ww.Krukenberg tumor: Krukenberg tumors are metastatic signet ring tumors, typically bilateral.
ww.Serous cystadenoma: Serous cystadenoma does not secrete hCG or AFP.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Embryonal carcinoma.

cards.tp: Aldosterone is driven by the renin-angiotensin system and hyperkalemia, not ACTH, so it is preserved. Failure to lactate (low prolactin), hypothyroid and adrenal symptoms follow pituitary infarction.

ww.Cortisol: Cortisol is low because ACTH falls when the pituitary is infarcted.
ww.Luteinizing hormone: LH is low from loss of gonadotropin secretion.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Aldosterone.

cards.tp: Brain death determination: exclude confounders, then test brainstem reflexes, then do the apnea test; ancillary tests only if these cannot be completed.

ww.Apnea test: The apnea test comes only after the brainstem reflexes are absent.
ww.Electroencephalography: EEG is an ancillary test, not a first step in brain death determination.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is D) Evaluation of brainstem reflexes.

bw: Best lab to screen for renal osteodystrophy?
cards.tp: CKD causes phosphate retention, low calcitriol and secondary hyperparathyroidism, giving osteitis fibrosa cystica; monitor PTH, calcium and phosphate.

ww.Erythrocyte sedimentation rate: ESR is nonspecific and does not assess bone turnover in CKD.
ww.C-reactive protein: CRP is an inflammation marker, not a bone marker.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Serum intact parathyroid hormone level.

cards.tp: Thyrotoxic myopathy causes proximal weakness with hyperreflexia; Graves disease gives suppressed TSH and elevated free T4.

ww.Anti-Mi-2 antibodies: Anti-Mi-2 antibodies mark dermatomyositis, which shows a rash and elevated CK.
ww.Elevated ESR: An elevated ESR suggests polymyalgia rheumatica or inflammation, not thyrotoxic myopathy.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Decreased thyroid-stimulating hormone.

bw: Pregnant, flank pain radiating to groin
cards.tp: Ultrasound is the first-line imaging for suspected nephrolithiasis in pregnancy; MRI or low-dose CT if inconclusive.

ww.Noncontrast CT: Noncontrast CT delivers fetal radiation and is second line in pregnancy.
ww.Renal radiograph: A plain radiograph exposes the fetus and misses many stones.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is B) Renal ultrasound.

cards.tp: ABCDE of melanoma: Asymmetry, Border irregularity, Color variegation, Diameter above 6 mm, Evolution.

ww.Symmetrical ovoid shape: Symmetry favors a benign nevus; melanoma is asymmetric.
ww.Smooth borders: Smooth, regular borders suggest a benign lesion; melanoma has irregular borders.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Different pigmentation throughout the lesion.

cards.tp: Start TMP-SMX when CD4 falls below 200. Toxoplasma prophylaxis begins below 100 (if IgG positive).

ww.Aspergillus fumigatus: Aspergillus prophylaxis is not recommended in HIV patients.
ww.Cytomegalovirus: CMV prophylaxis is not recommended at CD4 162.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is C) Pneumocystis jirovecii.

bw: Type 2 diabetes after failed lifestyle changes
cards.tp: Metformin is first line (unless contraindicated); intensify with SGLT2 inhibitor or GLP-1 agonist when cardiovascular or kidney disease exists.

ww.Glipizide: Sulfonylureas cause hypoglycemia and weight gain and are not first line.
ww.Basal insulin: Insulin is reserved for severe hyperglycemia or failure of other agents.

cards.evidence: The keyed answer is A) Metformin.

cards.tp: Large intrathoracic pressure swings in severe obstruction produce pulsus paradoxus (inspiratory SBP drop above 10 mmHg), a marker of severity; silent chest is ominous.
